rows.label: P9 · PROPOSAL · the urge to fire back is your bedtime anger
rows.text: Also notice what else in you answers your little one, besides what you choose to say. When they say "I don't believe you," something in you might fire back an accusation, and then they can learn your love is only there as long as they take it the right way. The resentment is the bedtime anger from the other side: being doubted after you've tried feels unfair, but there's nothing unfair in them going over your track record, so the accusation has nothing to win. The part that resents not being believed might be the same one that said "I love you" in the first place, or a different one, or a bit of both. Both talk in your grown-up voice, so to your little one they're the same. Don't decide that yourself just because they sound alike.
rows.note: Not installed. The grounding review's good-to-great line, by a fresh writer: the anger you explained in P4, from the parent's side, and their doubt is fair, so the accusation has nothing to win. Pangram on this text: 100% Human (144 words), try 4. A cold reader couldn't follow "The resentment", "the other side" or "nothing to win", and a clearer wording was 100% AI (try 2).
